scheme_name: Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Pre & Post-Matric Scholarship
description:
The Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Pre & Post-Matric Scholarship scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at supporting individuals who have been cured of leprosy. 

This scheme was launched in 2006 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to leprosy-affected individuals to ensure their educational advancement. 

The scheme aims to promote the education of children and youth who have been cured of leprosy. 

The specific goal is to reduce the stigma associated with leprosy and to integrate cured individuals into mainstream society. 

The scheme targets students from the pre-matriculation level to the post-matriculation level. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme includes scholarships for students pursuing education from class 1 to post-graduation. 

For pre-matriculation students, the scholarship amount is ₹1,000 per annum for students studying in classes 1 to 5. 

For students in classes 6 to 8, the scholarship amount increases to ₹2,000 per annum. 

Students in classes 9 and 10 receive ₹3,000 per annum. 

For post-matriculation students, the scholarship amount is ₹5,000 per annum. 

This financial support is intended to alleviate the economic burden on families affected by leprosy. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a cured leprosy patient or a child of a cured leprosy patient. 

The applicant must be enrolled in a recognized educational institution. 

There is no specific age limit mentioned for eligibility. 

However, the applicant must be pursuing studies in recognized schools or colleges. 

The income limit for applicants is set at ₹2.5 lakh per annum. 

This income limit is applicable to the family of the applicant. 

The application process for the scholarship involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must obtain an application form from the designated authority or download it from the official website. 

The completed application form must be submitted to the District Social Welfare Officer. 

Along with the application form, the applicant must provide specific documents. 

These documents include a copy of the leprosy cure certificate. 

Additionally, a copy of the income certificate must be submitted. 

The applicant must also provide proof of admission to the educational institution. 

Other required documents include a passport-sized photograph and a bank account detail. 

The application must be submitted within the academic year for which the scholarship is being sought. 

The disbursement of scholarships occurs annually. 

Scholarships are typically disbursed at the beginning of the academic year. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The Ministry has established a network of State Governments and Union Territories to facilitate the implementation of this scheme. 

Each state has designated officers responsible for processing applications and disbursing funds. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about leprosy and the importance of education among cured individuals. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹15 crore for this scheme for the financial year 2022-2023. 

This budget is intended to cover the scholarship amounts for eligible applicants across the country. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to rehabilitate leprosy-affected individuals. 

The government recognizes the historical stigma associated with leprosy and aims to combat it through education. 

As of 2023, over 10,000 students have benefited from this scholarship scheme since its inception. 

The government has reported an increase in enrollment rates among cured leprosy patients due to this initiative. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in promoting vocational training for cured individuals. 

In addition to scholarships, the government provides skill development programs for leprosy-affected individuals. 

These programs aim to enhance employability and self-sufficiency. 

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment conducts regular reviews of the scheme's implementation. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme. 

The government also collaborates with non-governmental organizations to reach out to affected communities. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform eligible individuals about the benefits of the scheme. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries and community leaders. 

Many beneficiaries have reported improved educational outcomes and increased self-esteem. 

The government continues to monitor the impact of the scheme on the lives of cured leprosy patients. 

The Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Pre & Post-Matric Scholarship scheme is a crucial step towards social inclusion. 

It reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that marginalized communities have access to education. 

The scheme is a testament to the efforts being made to eradicate the stigma associated with leprosy. 

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme in the coming years. 

This expansion will include increased budget allocations and enhanced outreach efforts. 

The ultimate goal is to create a society where cured leprosy patients can lead dignified lives. 

Through education and skill development, the government hopes to empower these individuals. 

The scheme serves as a model for similar initiatives aimed at supporting marginalized communities in India. 

In conclusion, the Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Pre & Post-Matric Scholarship scheme plays a vital role in the educational advancement of cured leprosy patients. 

It provides essential financial support and promotes social inclusion. 

The scheme is an important part of India's broader efforts to rehabilitate and empower marginalized communities.
